top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock (Katori and Ye) is a distinct physical advance over the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes: it makes the trap invisible to the clock transition so many atoms are interrogated Doppler- and recoil-free, turning the clock into a controlled many-body system. It is reproduced at the 10^-18 level by independent laboratories (JILA, RIKEN, SYRTE, PTB, NIST), and the two-name credit is agreed by all supporters; the citation should name the magic-wavelength lattice, not the accuracy figure or the future redefinition of the second. IceCube's diffuse flux is a mature discovery confirmed in several channels and ranks second, but the Halzen-Karle credit versus AMANDA and other leaders is unresolved. The topological insulator trio is strong science but omits Hasan and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal (Zhang deceased) and sits near the 2016 prize. Awarding something is better than no award.
recusal_note: No recusal needed for any proposal on this slate. As WACQT director and a superconducting-circuit theorist at Chalmers I would recuse from circuit QED and circuit-based quantum technology candidates, but none are in this slate; no apparent tie to Katori, Ye, Halzen, Karle, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp.
